items.justification: Cryptographic strength of authentication versus the permissions an AI system holds elsewhere.
Erasure of user data versus support offered during an incident.
Recording why a provision is unmet versus the required security content of model documentation.
Both build the operational record used to spot security problems, A by examining telemetry, B by logging system and user actions.
Confirmation of data deletion versus permissions granted on connected systems.
Both detect that the system is no longer behaving as intended, A through integrity alerting, B through log analysis for anomalies.
Transparency about absent updates versus re-testing after a major update.
Notifying users of a required update versus supporting them through an incident.
Both define the update support owed to the user; A covers what is published when updates are impossible, B the supply and delivery when they are not.
Both cut functionality that is not needed, A by enabling only required services, B by managing the risk of superfluous model capability.
Publishing a disclosure policy versus continuous infrastructure monitoring against risk appetite.
Physical interface exposure versus mitigating controls around poorly secured third-party components.
Uniqueness of security parameters versus transparency about data use and storage.
Recording justifications for unmet provisions versus publishing hashes for model components.
Presence of a secure update mechanism versus secure coding training.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus justifying use of poorly documented components.
Notifying users of a required update versus evaluation of access control frameworks.
Hardware mitigation of memory exploits and training that stops such flaws being written are distinct measures against one exploitation route.
Replaceable primitives and a working patch supply are separate preconditions for fixing a security weakness after deployment.
Both get security fixes onto the deployed product, A through an activated automatic mechanism, B through the supply and delivery chain.
Presence of a secure update mechanism versus communicating unresolvable threats downstream.
Validation of user interface input versus mitigating controls around poorly secured components.
Presence of a secure update mechanism versus separation of development environments.
Encryption of personal data in transit versus advance notice of model updates.
Deletion of personal data from services versus advance notice of model updates.
Cryptography for secure communication versus monitoring internal model states.
Tamper resistance of an identity and published hashes for components are distinct measures under one authenticity assurance.
Password uniqueness versus an organizational review of access control frameworks.
Cryptographic strength of authentication versus security testing before release.
Both recover from unauthorized modification through a known good state, which A's text names explicitly and B mandates outright.
Protection proportionate to risk and usage proportionate to data sensitivity are two sides of matching controls to what the data is worth.
Secure boot verification versus evaluating outputs for unintended influence over the system.
Publishing the support period versus contractual terms with cloud providers.
Secure storage of security parameters versus controls on an externally exposed model API.
Hardware memory access control versus maintaining an audit trail.
Both restrict use of a remotely reachable interface, A by requiring authentication, B by applying attack-mitigating controls.
User control over update notifications versus an audit log of configuration changes.
Erasure of user data versus security testing before release.
Reviewed cryptographic implementations versus monitoring model behaviour over time.
Machine-to-machine authentication method versus sharing test findings with operators.
